Three Directions for the Home Page

The same approved words, in the same order, in three different characters. One leads with the words, one with the people, one with the place. Open each one, scroll it on your phone as well, and say which one feels like this business.

A. The ClassifiedB. The Open SeatC. Main StreetThe site as it is now

What All Three Do That the Site Does Not Do Yet

  • The offer is in the first screen$100,000 minimum, no medical license, all 50 states, a limited number, a local office. Today a visitor has to scroll to assemble that.
  • Each is built on one thing you can seeA circled ad, an open seat beside a physician, a sign with a name on it. The current look is dark and glossy and could belong to a software company.
  • One button, said one waySee if I qualify, in the bar at the top, in the first screen and at the end.
  • The rules are keptNo earnings figures, no names that are not cleared, the FDA notice and the not-an-offer notice in place, the draft bar on.

For reference, the site as it is now. The words in the three directions below are the ones on this page today. Only the look and the order of the first screen change, so what you are comparing is the character.

A

A. The Classified

It leads with the words

Open A and scroll it

The page is set like the ad that found you: newsprint, a poster headline, and a red pencil around the three words that describe the reader. The typefaces are the ones in Regenerative Times, so the website, the magazine and the classified-style ads become one brand.

Clearest about
The offer in words. The headline is the biggest thing on the screen, and the terms sit beside it like the small print of an ad.
Why someone wants it
It reads like an opportunity that somebody circled and handed to them.
Strongest
On a phone, and for anyone arriving from a “Doctor seeks” ad. The page looks like the ad they clicked.
To know
It is the loudest of the three. The physician and the network numbers carry the reassurance.
B

B. The Open Seat

It leads with the people

Open B and scroll it

A clinic wall with two frames. One holds the medical director. The other is empty and says Owner Wanted. Under each hangs a brass plate, and the visitor can type a name onto the empty one. Green means the medicine and brass means the business, all the way down the page.

Clearest about
Who does what. The first screen is a picture of the headline, and it carries the line: Physicians own the medicine. You own the business around it.
Why someone wants it
The seat beside a named physician is open, and it can have their name on it.
Strongest
On trust, for a $100,000 decision. It suits practice owners and operators equally.
To know
Dr. Arora becomes the face of the first screen, so this one needs his yes. It is the quietest of the three.
C

C. Main Street

It leads with the place

Open C and scroll it

An office front drawn for this page: navy woodwork, a striped awning, gold lettering. The visitor types a name and a city. The sign changes, and the card in the window turns from Owner Wanted to Open.

Clearest about
What is being bought: a local business with the owner’s name on the sign.
Why someone wants it
They see their own name on it before they have filled in a form.
Strongest
With operators, and as a picture for ads. “The name on the sign is yours to choose” is already one of the eighteen.
To know
It is the friendliest and the least formal. Partners work from an office, which will not always be a shop front on a street.

What I Would Do

A for the whole site. It is the least like anything else in this market, it hits hardest, it is at its best on a phone, and it finishes the brand that the magazine and the classified-style ads started.

Inside it, use the idea from B: the two frames, as the picture that introduces the medical director, once he has agreed to it. Keep the sign from C for an ad and for the “Your name is on the sign” step.

If the team wants a quieter, more formal face for the site, B is the one, and A then becomes the look of the ad landing pages.

Say A, B, C or a mix. The site is built from one set of templates, so the direction you choose is applied to all 72 pages and the ad landing page together.

The words were not changed. Nothing typed into B or C is sent anywhere; it only changes the picture on that screen. Typefaces are open-licensed and travel with the page.
